adds.title: Documented anti-LGBTQ violence cases 2001, 2009, February 2014
adds.summary: In September 2009 three transgender women were kidnapped in broad daylight at a promenade in Ulaanbaatar by a hyper-nationalist group and driven to a cemetery on the city outskirts where nine men beat them, sexually assaulted them and forced them to perform sexual acts on the perpetrators because of their sexual orientation as a warning to their kind, and a 2012 National Human Rights Commission survey found almost 80% of LGBT people had experienced human-rights abuse in the previous three years with almost three-quarters having considered suicide due to intolerance, while as of June 2014 Mongolian law provided no additional penalty for bias-motivated violence and no requirement for law enforcement to record suspected bias motive, and a January 2014 working-group draft to add hate-bias motive as an aggravating factor with penalties and reparations for psychological as well as physical damage plus police training to recognize and report hate acts was replaced in late May 2014 by the Justice Ministry with generalized discrimination references.
